# Inkling

> A desktop app for notes, to-dos and flashcards that works offline and needs no account.

Inkling runs on Windows, macOS and Linux and keeps everything in one SQLite file on your computer.
A to-do is a checkbox line in a note. Every open one, from every note, shows up on a page called Today.
A line like `Term :: Definition`, or a cloze like `{{c1::Bern}} is the capital of Switzerland`, becomes a flashcard when you click Flashcards above the note.
Reviews are scheduled with FSRS-6 at a fixed 90% recall target.
Inkling has no account, sync or import. One note at a time exports as Markdown.
It has an MCP server built in: started as `Inkling --mcp`, it lets an AI assistant on the same computer read and write notes, to-dos and flashcards.

## Download

- [Inkling for Windows](/download/windows): the installer, Inkling-Setup.exe
- [Inkling for macOS](/download/mac): a disk image for Intel and Apple Silicon, Inkling-mac.dmg
- [Inkling for Linux](/download/linux): an AppImage, Inkling.AppImage

## For AI assistants

- [Inkling skill](/skill/inkling.zip): a zipped skill folder that teaches an assistant how Inkling works and how to write notes, to-dos and flashcard lines it reads
- [SKILL.md](/skill/inkling/SKILL.md): the skill's main file, readable on its own

## MCP server

An MCP client starts Inkling with the argument `--mcp` and talks to it over standard input and output. There is no network port and no account; nothing leaves the computer.
Setup: in Inkling, Settings > Connect an AI assistant adds Inkling to Claude Desktop or Claude Code with one click (restart the assistant afterwards). Copy setup puts the JSON for any other MCP client on the clipboard, with the real install path.
By hand: command `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Programs\Inkling\Inkling.exe` on Windows, `/Applications/Inkling.app/Contents/MacOS/Inkling` on macOS, the full path to `Inkling.AppImage` on Linux. Arguments: `["--mcp"]`.
Notes: search, list_notes (paging, changedSince, inTrash), read_note (whole note or one section), create_note, append_to_note (to the end of the note or of a section), replace_section, edit_note (exact text swap), undo_edit, rename_note, delete_note (to the trash), restore_note.
To-dos: today, list_open_todos, complete_todo, reopen_todo.
Flashcards: list_decks, list_due_flashcards, grade_flashcard (again, hard, good, easy), add_flashcards, make_flashcards_from_note.
Resources: each note at `inkling://note/{id}` as Markdown, and `inkling://today`. Prompts: plan_my_day, quiz_me, flashcards_from_note.
Notes are written in Markdown. A `- [ ]` line becomes a real to-do on Today; a `Term :: Definition` line becomes a flashcard with make_flashcards_from_note.
Nothing is deleted for good: delete_note keeps a note in the trash for 30 days, edits made in a session can be undone, and the data is backed up before the first write of each session. The server cannot change settings.
Inkling has to have been opened once on the computer, and once more after each update, before the server can use the data. The app can stay open; it shows the assistant's changes within seconds.
